name: A succession crisis
about: An old lord falls sick, and his heir is weak or young. An ambitious bannerman circles. The heir is confirmed, ruled for, locked up or driven out, depending on the house's men and how the crown treats them.
title: The {old.houseName} Succession
fade: The talk about who rules {old.houseName} dies down. {thread} becomes something for scholars to argue over.

beats.speaker: old
beats.text: {old} of {old.house} takes to {old.his} bed with a fever that won't break. In {hall}, men count the days and look at {heir}, then at each other.

memory.heir: My {old.father} is sick, and the bannermen look at me as if I were already a problem.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {claimant} rides to {hall} with more men than a visit needs, and asks loudly how {old} is doing.

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: {old} dies in {hall} with {heir}'s hand in {old.his}. The whole household waits.

memory.heir: My {old.father} died holding my hand. Now everyone watches what I do.

die.how: I died in my bed at {hall}, with {heir} beside me.

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: {old} is dead, and the seat at {hall} passes to {heir}. Nobody looks at {heir}. Everyone looks at {claimant}.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {claimant} offers to rule {old.house} until {heir} is grown. The household knights stare at their boots.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {claimant} takes the keys of {hall} at night. {heir} is kept "safe" in the north tower, as {claimant} puts it. Not every town will have {claimant}: those loyal to {heir} shut their gates.

memory.heir: {claimant} stole the keys of {hall} and locked me in the tower.

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: {heir} climbs down the wall of {hall} on a rope of bedsheets and rides to Kingsmere to ask the crown for justice.

court.text: {heir}, in torn clothes, kneels before the throne: "{claimant} holds {hall} and my father's towns are at war over it. My towns stand for me, Your Grace. Stand with them."

options.label: Ride with {heir} and take back {hall}
options.hint: {heir.houseName} restored under {heir} · the towns that rose go back to their house
options.result: The crown's riders saddle at dawn, {heir} at their head.

options.label: Let {heir} keep the towns that stood for {heir}
options.hint: a lesser house of {heir}'s own · {claimant} keeps {hall}
options.result: The King lets the towns that rose keep {heir} as their lord.

options.label: The crown will not take sides
options.hint: the rising settles itself: the side with more towns keeps them
options.result: The King sends {heir} away with a purse and no promise.

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: The crown's riders come to {hall} with {heir} leading them. {claimant} hands back the keys and is thrown out of {old.house}'s lands with nothing but {claimant.his} horse.

memory.claimant: I held {hall} for a season and lost it to a child and the King's riders.
memory.heir: The King gave me back {hall}. I will not forget who took it.

claimant.text: take back what {heir} and the King took from me

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: {old.houseName} is two houses now. {claimant} holds {hall}; the towns that rose for {heir} keep {heir} as their lord, by the King's leave.

memory.heir: The King let me keep the towns that stood by me. Not my father's hall, but mine.
memory.claimant: I hold {hall}, and the King gave half my house to a child.

beats.speaker: heir
beats.text: The King won't hear {heir}. {claimant} rules {old.house} from {hall}, and {heir} is the rightful {heir.lord} but has no home.

memory.heir: {claimant} stole my father's seat, and the King did nothing.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {claimant} rules {old.house} from {hall}. One by one the bannermen kneel, and {heir} is never seen outside the tower.
The bannermen of {old.house} meet in {hall} and swear loyalty to {heir}, with {claimant} to advise until {heir.he} is grown. {claimant} signs last.

memory.claimant: The bannermen swore for {heir}. I signed last, and they all saw it.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {claimant} kneels before {heir} in {hall} and swears loyalty. Whatever {claimant.he} wanted, {claimant.he} wants a clean name more.

beats.speaker: claimant
beats.text: {heir} is dead, and {claimant} is the strongest {claimant.man} left in {old.house}. Nobody asks how the {heir.son} died, because nobody dares.

claimant.text: be named lord of {old.house} when the time comes

beats.text: {claimant} is dead, and {thread} dies with {claimant.him}. {heir} keeps the seat at {hall}, but it isn't easy.
